chunks: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Abu Thabit from Hanan from Ibn Abi Ya'fur from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār said:

A mawla (client) of ʿAlī (peace be upon him) died, so he said: 'Look, do you find an heir for him?' It was said to him: 'Two daughters in al-Yamāmah, who were enslaved.' So he purchased them from the deceased's wealth, then handed over the remainder of the wealth to them.

key_terms.بَقِيَّةَ اَلْمَالِ: The remainder of the wealth, after specific deductions or purchases.
key_terms.مَمْلُوكَتَانِ: Two enslaved women, dependents who are part of the estate's assets.
key_terms.وارثاً: Heir, one who inherits the estate.
key_terms.وَلِيٌّ: Mawla (client/freedman), a person who has been freed by another or has a patronage relationship.

ai.seo_question: How is the estate of a mawla distributed if they have no direct heirs according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Imam’s role as the heir of the mawla, specifically illustrating the practical application of freeing enslaved dependents from the deceased’s estate before distributing the remainder. It underscores the Shia legal principle that the Imam’s inheritance rights extend to the mawla’s property, ensuring their social and economic liberation as part of the estate settlement.
